p: Planetary imaging for PixInsight, with two processes. SERViewer opens SER video files and uncompressed 8-bit greyscale or raw Bayer AVI files (such as ASIAIR captures): it shows any frame in a preview, opens it as a PixInsight image, and can save an AVI as a SER file. PlanetaryStack stacks such a video into one image (lucky imaging): it measures every frame, chooses the sharpest frames and aligns them, region by region, with nothing to set, previews the stack with zoom, and opens it as a new image, or says why a capture gives none. The target is read from the ASIAIR file name, and for a colour capture of the Moon not taken through a narrowband or IR-pass filter PlanetaryStack can also make a mineral moon (calibrated, sharpened, with the Moon's true colour differences amplified), tuned live with Strength, Chroma blur and Sharpen sliders. New in 0.5: for a colour capture of Mercury to Neptune not taken through a narrowband or IR-pass filter, Planet processing makes a finished image in the planet's natural colour (calibrated to its catalogue reflectance, red and blue aligned against atmospheric dispersion, shown linear and sharpened), tuned live with Saturation, Chroma blur and Sharpen sliders.

Both read only the video file you choose and an AVI's .txt sidecar. SERViewer writes only the SER file you choose; either process writes, if you click Save pattern..., the .txt sidecar next to the AVI. Neither uses the network or runs external programs. Documentation: doc/tools/SERViewer/SERViewer.html and doc/tools/PlanetaryStack/PlanetaryStack.html.
